speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: It's just me on the desk this morning, so bear with me while I answer the phones myself.

speaker: Dougal Thomson
text: Dougal Thomson, Portobello. It's the bins. Three weeks now and nobody's lifted them, and the gulls have found out.

speaker: Dougal Thomson
text: Aye, I'll keep it short. I've been trying since the news.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Dougal Thomson in Portobello. Dougal, the bins.

speaker: Dougal Thomson
text: Three weeks, Eilidh. Three weeks of bags on the pavement, and the gulls having a festival. I've rung the council, I've rung the councillor, and now I'm ringing you.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: We'll ask them. Thanks, Dougal.

speaker: Flora Armstrong
text: Flora Armstrong, Musselburgh. Och, I've no question really, Shona. I just love the show and I wanted to say so.

speaker: Alastair Buchanan
text: Alastair. I've a thing or two to say about that presenter of yours, and I'll be saying them on air, so just put me through.

speaker: Tavish
text: It's Tavish. Aye, I know what it says on your screen. That was months ago. I just want a word about the ferries.

speaker: Tavish
text: Me again. Come on, Shona, it's one word about the ferries.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Coming up after the news: Gregor Stewart and the last tram down Leith Walk. Stay with us.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Morning. If you can hear this, you're in the room with me: listeners are still on the overnight log.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: That's the overnight done. Kettle FM is live, the kettle's on, and Steeped follows after the news.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Iona MacIntosh is on the line from Derry. Iona, go ahead.

speaker: Iona MacIntosh
text: Morning, Eilidh. It's the ferry fares. They've gone up twice this year, the timetable's got worse, and if you miss the last one you're sleeping in the car.

speaker: Iona MacIntosh
text: …can you hear me? Hello? The signal's awful on this stretch of road, I'll… the fares, I was saying…

speaker: Iona MacIntosh
text: Sorry about that, Eilidh, I'm back. Where was I: the fares. Twice this year.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Thanks, Iona. Safe home.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: It's nearly ten on Kettle FM. Finlay Grant has Steeped after this, and he'll be joining me in a wee while.

speaker: Finlay Grant
text: One, two. One, two. Is that loud enough, or am I too close to it?

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Finlay, it's Eilidh. You sound good. I'll bring you on at five to, we'll have a wee chat, then it's yours.

speaker: Finlay Grant
text: Five to. Right you are. I'll have my first record ready.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: That's nearly it from me this morning. Thanks for all your calls about Leith Walk, and to Gregor for the trams.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Finlay, you're on after this. In three, two, one.

speaker: Finlay Grant
text: Ready when you are.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: And here he is. Finlay Grant, good morning. What's in the pot for Steeped today?

speaker: Finlay Grant
text: Morning, Eilidh. Morning, everyone. Loose leaf and long records: an hour of Scottish folk you'll not have heard on the radio.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Lovely. That's me away, then. Finlay, she's all yours.

speaker: Finlay Grant
text: This is Steeped on Kettle FM, with me, Finlay Grant. The kettle's still on. Here's the first one.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Good morning, this is The Morning Kettle on Kettle FM. No phones this morning: one guest, and he is on his way.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Gregor, it's Eilidh, off air. Two more minutes when we come back: the depot at Shrubhill.

speaker: Gregor Stewart
text: Shrubhill. Right you are.

speaker: Gregor Stewart
text: The depot at Shrubhill is where they went to be broken up. There is a block of flats on it now, and not one plaque.

speaker: Eilidh Fraser-MacLeod
text: Gregor Stewart, thank you. That was the last tram down Leith Walk.
